body_ar: السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته، بالنسبة للتسويق الشبكي له صور كثيرة لكن المباح منها هو أن يكون الإنسان سمسارا لبضاعة معينة فهو يشتريها لنفسه لحاجته إليها ولا يشتريها من أجل مجرد التشجيع الذي سيعطى عليها بل يشتريها ليستعملها ثم هو يدل الآخرين عليها فإذا جاء بواحد كان له نقطة وإذا جاء باثنين وهكذا بعشرة بمائة، وكل واحد من أولئك أيضا له نقطة إذا أتى بزبون وهكذا هذه لا حرج فيها لأنها بمثابة السمسرة والدلالة على البضاعة وهي نفع يصل إلى منتج البضاعة و "من أسدى نفعا إلى غيره حيث لا يجب عليه فله أجرة المثل"، وأجرة المثل إذا كان الشيء متفقا عليه من قبل فإن المتفق عليه يغني عن أجرة المثل. اضغط هنا لمشاهدة الفتوى
body_en:
Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

As regards network marketing, it has many forms; but the permissible (mubāḥ) one among them is that a person act as a broker for a particular commodity. He buys it for himself because he needs it, and does not buy it merely for the sake of the inducement that will be given him for it; rather he buys it in order to use it, and then he directs others to it. If he brings in one person he has a point, and if he brings in two, and so on — ten, a hundred; and each one of those likewise has a point if he brings in a customer, and so on.

There is no objection in this, because it stands in the place of brokerage (samsarah) and of directing people to a commodity, and it is a benefit that reaches the producer of the commodity. And "whoever renders a benefit to another where it was not obligatory upon him is entitled to the going rate (ajr al-mithl)". As for the going rate: if the thing was agreed upon beforehand, then what was agreed upon dispenses with the going rate.

flags.arabic: له صور كثيرة لكن المباح منها هو أن يكون الإنسان سمسارا لبضاعة معينة
options: he rules on one form only and says nothing about the others
he implies that the form he describes is the only permissible one
he is permitting network marketing generally
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The Sheikh says network marketing has many forms and then describes the permissible one, with two conditions built into the description: the buyer must need the goods, and must not buy them merely to earn the referral inducement. He does not rule on any other form and does not say what makes the others impermissible. Published in English under the bare title 'Network Marketing', this will be read as a general permission for multi-level marketing, which is not what the text says. It needs the qualification displayed with it, or the Sheikh's office should supply his ruling on the other forms.

flags.arabic: "من أسدى نفعا إلى غيره حيث لا يجب عليه فله أجرة المثل"
options: a legal maxim (qāʿidah) quoted without attribution
a quotation from a named jurist
flags.note: The source puts it in quotation marks with no attribution. It reads as a juristic maxim, not a hadith, and the English keeps it in quotation marks without introducing it as a prophetic report, which would be an attribution the Sheikh did not make. A reviewer should identify the source.

flags.context: فله أجرة المثل، وأجرة المثل إذا كان الشيء متفقا عليه من قبل فإن المتفق عليه يغني عن أجرة المثل
options: the customary fee for comparable work
flags.note: Technical term: the fee a comparable service would command, used where no fee was agreed. Not in the project glossary; a candidate for addition. The closing sentence is elliptical in the Arabic — 'and the going rate, if the thing was agreed beforehand…' — and the English straightens it without adding to it.

translator_notes: التشجيع is rendered 'the inducement': the commission or bonus offered for recruiting, which is the thing the Sheikh says must not be the buyer's motive.
نقطة is rendered literally as 'a point' because that is the scheme's own term and the Sheikh uses it without comment.
